hints: Notice the $5.0 \text{ g}$ pellet at $200 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ sticks in the stationary $95 \text{ g}$ block, so first find their common velocity just after impact.
Apply conservation of linear momentum with total mass $100 \text{ g}$ because the impact is perfectly inelastic and external impulse is negligible.
Then convert the post-impact kinetic energy of the combined $100 \text{ g}$ mass into gravitational potential energy $mgh$ to find the rise height $h$.
walkthrough: Convert masses to kilograms: $m = 0.0050 \text{ kg}$ and $M = 0.095 \text{ kg}$, so total mass is $0.10 \text{ kg}$.
Use conservation of momentum for embedding: $mv = (m+M)V$.
Substitute $0.0050 \times 200 = 0.10 \times V$, giving $V = 1.0/0.10 = 10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ just after impact.
Use energy conservation for the free rise: $\frac{1}{2}(m+M)V^2 = (m+M)gh$, so $h = V^2/(2g)$.
Substitute $V = 10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$: $h = 100/19.62 \approx 5.1 \text{ m}$. This is option A.
